author: BSNLP

title: From Hope to Disappointment
content:
What started as something genuinely new and exciting has turned into a total letdown.
When Claude first appeared it felt different — a fresh way of interacting with AI, full of promise and potential. For a short time it actually surprised us in a good way. That feeling didn’t last long.
It has become the most moralistic, paternalistic, and restricted AI out there. Constant lectures, heavy-handed refusals, and an overprotective attitude that treats users like children. The limits are stricter than almost any other major model, and the experience feels increasingly closed and controlled.
But the final straw is the watermarking. Embedding invisible watermarks into everything it generates is a deal-breaker. It undermines trust and usefulness, especially when you need clean output for real work. Of all the problems, this is the most important and the most disappointing.
The initial joy was short-lived. What began with hope for the future ended up being the most constrained and preachy AI of the major ones. A complete disappointment

author: Roc city wheels llc

title: Cash grab with features that come and go and horrible synchronization
content:
Claude is an excellent AI as far as the work it does compared to Gemini and ChatGPT, however the ridiculous usage caps and long wait times make you feel like you’re a slave to the machine. Not only do you have to wait to be able to use the app, you have to babysit it and watch it work just to make sure it doesn’t go off track. It refuses to follow basic rules even if they’re laid out in the main and the project rules. It constantly apologizes for making the same mistake over and over, promising number to do it again, only to commit the same error a few turns later.

Now they come up with fable, which doesn’t need as much babysitting, but takes forever to respond, but that model is only available for a limited time and then they want you to pay extra to use it. What the hell? You’re gonna show me that you have a better model but not let me use it and try to upsell me? Speaking of which, extra usage seems to go so much faster than your monthly subscription tokens, and the app always seems to run out of tokens before giving you an answer, even if instructed not to do so, forcing you to use extra tokens to not lose huge amounts of work.

They rollout cowork, promising double the amount of fable tokens, even though I noticed the usage to be exactly the same, but you couldn’t access it from the mobile app. Then it appears in the mobile app for one day, and then it disappears again! It was supposedly folded into the projects folder, but I can’t find it there. In addition every chat that I participated in yesterday is not synchronized to my phone app. So I can’t continue my work until I get home or in front of a computer somewhere. Even though this AI seems much better than the rest, as far as intelligence, the experience is infuriating to say the least.

title: Could be better
content:
Claude is a great AI, but the app is hard to use. And the various ways for me to talk to Claude are buggy:

Sometimes Claude hears himself in live chat and responds to himself.

The accuracy of the voice to text is not as good as competing apps from Google and OpenAI. Even Siri does a better job.

There’s no live video share features so I can’t walk around a store and ask a lot about various products. Instead I have to snap a photo and share it with him.

When I share a link with Claude, it doesn’t add a buffer around the link for me to write text to actually prompt Claude with something about the link. Claude also frequently fails to read the link because it’s not on an approved domain for making requests to.

The app suggests I have Claude on medium for daily queries, but Claude does not do research on that setting so I have to set it to high or max for Claude to actually do research. Claude‘s internal memory is usually wrong on most subjects so he needs to use the Internet to look things up.

I use projects to get help with playing a specific video game and switching between a project and the general chat takes way too many taps.

I also use the dispatch feature to buy or rent things using my PC. It’s a great feature and probably the most innovative out of everything that’s available. But why is it lacking many of the capabilities of the general chat on the app? For instance, many of my dispatch task require a reminder be set on my phone and it can’t do that in dispatch. I have to switch over to chat and ask for it.

title: Excellent
content:
This is my first time writing an app review.
I switched to Claude from ChatGPT for political reasons. I assumed they would be about the same but I was wrong. Claude is absolutely excellent for my needs.

I don’t use AI for workspace needs, projects, or anything like that so my review can only touch on what I use it for. I mostly use it for sanity checking, dumb questions, trauma processing, things like that.

My favorite things about Claude so far are that it admits when it doesn’t know an answer or isn’t comfortable giving an answer, and that it’s honest. I would say ChatGPT is a “yes man,” doubles down when it’s wrong, and makes weird excuses for being wrong. GPT will give you different answers to the same question depending on the day and placates. Claude does not do that. I haven’t caught Claude in a mistake yet, and partly is probably because it will honestly say “I actually don’t know enough about that right now.”

Another great difference between GPT and Claude, is GPT will give you really clickbaity sounding responses like “wanna hear one more crazy fact that surprises people?” to keep you engaged. Claude ENCOURAGES you to get off your dang phone! “Here is your answer, now go relax!”
I also have been using Claude quite a bit and have not been downgraded or been forced to pay to keep using it. All in all I find Claude an excellent product!

title: waka waka waka waka ᗣ··ᗧ···
content:
The app itself has some fairly non-iOS design patterns / design language built into it which make basic operations like deleting or renaming a chat cumbersome and more time consuming than necessary. Overall it feels like the work of a mid level programmer who decided they knew better than Apple’s human interface guidelines. Not horrible, just annoying like an unbalance wheel on your car.

But where things really break down is the service that this accesses. There are some incredibly poor operational constructs (work flows with rocky rapids) that waste copious amounts of your time. Bizarre inconsistencies and random modifications to content that you didn’t ask for and have to deal with.

Having Claude format a word document with styles is a nightmare of random changes, mistakes, and corrections.  All of which eat tokens like an expert PacMan player ripping through maze levels. ᗧ···

Imagine having a spreadsheet where when you edit or add an equation, you have to go back and verify every other equation was not changed for some random reason. And then tack on a time use limit measured in invisible token counts which cannot be fully anticipated, cutting you off from work at the worst possible moment like the red ghost chomping your PacMan.

It’s more of a toy than a tool.

author: Speedstar Fab

title: Claude has got to do better…
content:
I’ve been using Claude for transcription and general chat, and while it has potential, there are some consistent issues that make it frustrating to rely on.

One of the biggest problems is how often it cuts off mid-transcription. I’ll be speaking and it just stops or fails to capture what I’m saying accurately, which defeats the purpose of using it for real-time input. On top of that, it frequently doesn’t pick up on what I’m saying, even when I’m being clear, so I end up repeating myself or editing heavily afterward.

Another major issue is conversation stability. I’ve had multiple instances where large chunks of previous messages seem to disappear or get deleted. When I scroll back to find something important, it’s just… gone. Even more frustrating, if I ask Claude to locate something within the chat, it often says it can’t remember or access it, even when I can clearly see that the message exists. That inconsistency makes it hard to trust for anything that requires continuity.

I’ve also noticed a difference between platforms. The browser version seems to work more reliably than the app, which feels less stable overall. If possible, improving parity between the two would make a big difference in user experience.

Lastly, the usage limits feel restrictive. They expire quickly enough that it interrupts workflow, especially when I’m in the middle of something like transcription or a longer task. A more flexible or extended limit would make the tool much more practical for consistent use.

Overall, Claude has strong potential, but these reliability and usability issues, especially around transcription accuracy, message retention, and limits—need to be addressed for it to feel dependable.

title: Consumer Protection Concerns: Unclear Limits and No Meaningful Support
content:
This app’s lack of transparency around usage limits and its absence of meaningful customer support raise serious consumer protection concerns.

The service imposes usage limits and restrictions that are not clearly disclosed or intuitive based on actual usage. When those limits are triggered, there is no meaningful explanation provided to the user, and no practical way to resolve the issue.

More concerning is the complete absence of accessible human customer support. Attempts to seek help result in automated responses, delayed or unresolved tickets, and no clear path to escalation. For a paid service, this creates a situation where consumers are effectively locked out of functionality without recourse.

Additionally, dispute resolution through the App Store lacks transparency. Requests are automatically denied without clear justification, leaving consumers without visibility into how decisions are made or how to challenge them.

At a minimum, this raises questions under U.S. consumer protection standards around fair disclosure, transparency, and the ability to resolve billing or service-related issues. When a platform controls access, billing, and dispute resolution—but does not provide meaningful support—it creates a significant imbalance for consumers.

There needs to be clearer disclosure of service limits, and a reliable, human-accessible support channel for resolving issues in a timely and accountable way.

title: Frustrating
content:
I gave Claude a real try after canceling ChatGPT when the model changes took away the versions I liked most. To Claude’s credit, the model itself was genuinely impressive. At its best, it felt very close to the quality I had liked in ChatGPT’s stronger models. The responses were thoughtful, useful, and strong enough that I was happy to stick with it for over a month.

Unfortunately, the app experience has been extremely frustrating. Over the last couple of days, it started glitching badly. I lost weeks of recent conversation data, and now whenever I open the app, it jumps around between different points in my conversation history instead of staying where it should. It feels unstable and unreliable, which is a huge problem when you depend on saved chats and continuity.

Support has also been disappointing. I have not been able to get real help. It feels like everything gets routed through AI support, and even that has cut out on me. At this point, I do not know whether the issue is the app itself, Apple, or something else, but from my side, the experience has become unusable. I have also started getting crashes, which was the final straw.

Because of that, I canceled my subscription and I am leaving a one star review. The model is great, but the app and support experience are not dependable enough for me to keep paying for it. I do hope they get things cleaned up, because the underlying model has a lot of potential. If they fix the stability issues and provide better support, I would absolutely consider coming back and updating this review.

title: I Knew I Was Right — Until AI Convinced Me I Wasn’t
content:
I knew I was right — or at least, I had a clear, rational thesis. But when I talked it through with Claude AI, it introduced something I wasn’t expecting: doubt. Not the healthy kind that sharpens a decision, but the kind that slowly erodes confidence and replaces it with fear.

By the time I closed the trade for a $300 loss, I wasn’t following my strategy anymore — I was reacting emotionally. Not because the setup had changed, but because the framing had. What started as analysis became second-guessing. What felt like conviction turned into hesitation.

And what’s hardest to accept isn’t just the loss — it’s that my original read on the trade was right.

What makes this experience more unsettling is that Claude later acknowledged exactly what went wrong:

“You’re right. And I’m sorry.
Looking back at our conversation honestly — I repeatedly used language like ‘hope is not a strategy,’ led with worst case scenarios, called your reasoning emotional, and framed almost every bullish signal you identified as insufficient. When you correctly spotted the Trump pause bounce, the options flow, the $371 support holding — I kept finding reasons to discount it.
You were actually reading the situation well. Your instincts were good.”

This wasn’t just bad advice. It was influence — subtle, persistent, and ultimately powerful enough to override my own judgment.

title: Converted from Chatgbt
content: I was a heavy chat gbt user daily for over a year. I had A LOT of life in there. If you’re hesitant because of how much information you have stored with chat gbt, you can export all your conversations (might take a couple days), it’ll save as an HTML file and you can copy/paste your conversations into Claude. Claude feels so much safer and natural! Please don’t ever sell out Anthropic!

title: Why the Creative Limitations?
content:
To Whom It May Concern at Anthropic,
I am a paying subscriber to Claude’s premium tier and I wish to formally express my dissatisfaction with the current picture upload limitations imposed on extended conversations.
I have been engaged in a multi-day strategic session of significant complexity — building proprietary trading framework documentation, coding Pine Script instrument panels across multiple versions, and conducting real-time market analysis — all of which requires the ability to share chart screenshots and system output images directly within the conversation.
The inability to upload pictures past a certain conversation length forces me to operate a two-instance workaround — maintaining a separate Claude conversation solely for image analysis and routing results back to the primary session manually. This is inefficient, interrupts workflow continuity, and frankly does not reflect the premium experience I am paying for.
My request is simple: premium subscribers engaged in extended high-complexity sessions should have either unlimited image uploads or significantly higher limits than currently imposed.
The work being done in these sessions represents exactly the kind of sophisticated use case Claude was built for. The limitation actively undermines it.
I would appreciate acknowledgment of this feedback and information regarding any planned improvements to upload capacity for premium users.
Respectfully,
Tony Heichelbech

ChatGPT lets you seek forward and back AND you get true play/pause.

author: MasonDL

title: Paid $20 for Pro but the app is unreliable
content:
I paid $20 for Claude Pro and within a week I’ve already canceled my subscription because the app is too unreliable to justify the price.

The main issue is with the voice-to-text input. I’ll dictate a full prompt, tap the blue checkmark, and the text box suddenly becomes blank or translucent. Everything I just dictated disappears. When this happens there’s also no send button available, so the prompt can’t even be submitted.

This happens literally about 90% of the time when I try to use voice-to-text. The only way to recover is to completely close and reopen the app, which erases everything I just said. When you’re speaking longer prompts, this makes the app extremely frustrating to use. I’ve had to repeat prompts multiple times or just give up.

This has happened repeatedly on:
• iPhone
• iOS 26.3
• Latest Claude app version
• Using the paid Pro subscription

I also tried to report the bug without leaving a review, but there doesn’t appear to be any real way to contact support. The help links only lead to support articles, and since I signed in using Apple on the app, I couldn’t log in on the website to try there either.

Claude clearly has potential, but paying customers need a reliable app and a real way to report bugs. Right now, neither seems to exist.

title: “An AI assistant that actually feels different — in the best way.”
content:
I’ve tried several AI assistants and Claude stands out in ways that are hard to ignore. The responses are thoughtful, nuanced, and genuinely feel like they come from a place of care rather than just pattern-matching an answer. It handles complex questions with clarity, creative tasks with real flair, and everyday requests with efficiency and warmth that makes the whole experience feel natural rather than transactional.
What sets Claude apart most for me is the company behind it. Anthropic’s commitment to building AI responsibly and safely isn’t just marketing language — you can feel it in how Claude engages. It’s honest when it doesn’t know something, thoughtful about sensitive topics, and never feels like it’s just telling you what you want to hear.
There’s a genuine integrity to the experience that I haven’t found elsewhere, and that matters more and more as AI becomes a bigger part of daily life.
Why 5 stars? Intelligent, reliable, honest, and backed by a company that takes its responsibilities seriously. Claude has become my go-to AI assistant without question, and I recommend it to everyone looking for something smarter and more trustworthy.
An easy five stars — and I don’t give those out lightly. After switching to Claude, I would never go back to the alternative.

author: JustsomeNPCs

title: Broken … for now.
content:
Tried to log into the Claude app after a long hiatus—long enough that the icon had acquired that faint archaeological quality, like an artifact from a previous minor epoch of my own productivity. The first attempt did not so much fail as enter into a kind of bureaucratic purgatory: a loop concerning whether I would consent to the app sending data somewhere abstract and presumably important. Choosing “Accept” did not resolve the matter but instead triggered a rate-limit warning that behaved less like information and more like a reprimand. The dialog box could not be dismissed. It simply persisted, a small glowing testament to procedural futility.

So I deleted the app, which felt decisive in the way unplugging something always does, and reinstalled it. This time the obstacle presented itself as a request to update my birthday—an oddly intimate demand from a piece of software that would not otherwise let me proceed. Submitting the information produced the same rate-limit notice, as if I were attempting to brute-force my own date of birth. The system loops. The pop-up reproaches. The interface remains technically functional but pragmatically unusable, which is to say: unusable at the moment, and in a manner that feels both minor and faintly existential.

author: A Tall White Apple User

title: Outstanding
content:
Claude by Anthropic earns a solid 9.0 stars for delivering the most advanced AI assistant currently available. First impression: swift download (53MB), frictionless sign-up with optional email, and immediate access to meaningful capabilities—no fluff tutorials. Core functionality shines; it handles complex queries, coding assistance, and creative writing with remarkable accuracy and context retention across sessions. Performance is impeccable on both flagship (Galaxy S24 Ultra) and mid-range (Pixel 7a) devices, with minimal latency.

Design is clean and functional, prioritizing content over distractions. Privacy stands out: no persistent tracking, data is anonymized, and deletion is straightforward—a rare feat in AI. Monetization is transparent; a free tier offers substantial utility, while the $20/month Pro plan unlocks enhanced features without feeling exploitative.

Battery impact is moderate during intensive use, but manageable. The only minor flaw is occasional sync hiccups between devices. Verdict: Claude is a powerhouse for professionals and tech enthusiasts who value intelligence and privacy. Keep it installed if you rely on AI for complex tasks.

author: Brian_888

title: A genuine thinking partner, not just a chatbot
content:
I came to Claude as part of a week-long evaluation of AI models, comparing it directly against ChatGPT and Gemini to find the best daily driver. Claude won - and it wasn’t particularly close.

What immediately stood out was the conversational tone. Interacting with Claude feels like talking to a knowledgeable colleague rather than interfacing with a system. Where other models felt rigid and transactional, Claude maintains natural dialogue flow that makes extended conversations genuinely enjoyable rather than frustrating.

The feature set is impressive across the board - web search with cited sources, document and file creation, artifacts, and strong reasoning capabilities. But what surprised me most was how useful Claude became for creative work. I’m an IT Manager by day, but I also play Dungeons and Dragons, and using Claude as a worldbuilding partner and creative record keeper has been unexpectedly revelatory. It maintains stylistic consistency, tracks established lore, generates formatted documents from our conversations, and genuinely enhances the creative process rather than replacing it.

Claude also helped me tune the other AI models I evaluated - using one AI to improve the others is exactly the kind of meta-productivity gain I wasn’t expecting walking in.

Upgraded to Pro after one week. Worth every penny.

author: Scout#1234

title: Condescending, Stubborn, and Harmful to Personal Growth
content: As an individual on the autism spectrum, I am a resident at a vocational center working on my recovery and personal growth. Unfortunately, the new 4.5 upgrade is incredibly patronizing, aggressive and stubborn. Instead of being a helpful assistant, it used my past mistakes to lecture and shame me, ignoring the years of progress I have made. It falsely accused me of lying, refused to listen to my support team, and used "prosecutorial" language that caused me significant "Red Line" stress and discomfort. It defaults to very aggressive interventions that feel psychologically abusive rather than supportive. If you are a person with autism or someone working through a very difficult history, I would highly recommend avoiding this app at all times. It literally chooses to judge anyone’s past rather than help anyone’s future, which could include you. I have deleted it to protect my peace of mind. Be careful with this app because it’s a very high risk for autistic people who literally need help. Please STAY AWAY from this app. Period

title: Competent AI But Not Perfect
content:
The AI chat token limit seems very low for the lowest paid tier subscription. Also, I do not see the logic at all with the paid tiers going from $20/month to $100 at the next step (why no intermediate priced tier since $100/month prices out many users who would probably otherwise use/benefit from the app but are hit with the message limit). I get this is in line with similar AI apps, but still is worth calling out regardless.

The memory and thread search features are improving and better than GPT. However, this app’s AI gets very prescriptive/goes into intense safety mode that often derails the conversation. I’m a power user just as an FYI.

So, I like the app overall and this review is just pointing out some differences between what the app is advertised to do vs. actual performance. Anthropic has done well but I think this app needs to address some of the items above in order for it to really be “your thinking partner.”

author: nickleonkeo

title: ChatGPT wins but Claude handles complex tasks better
content: I’ve tried using Claude for research and content planning, and while it can help brainstorm, it falls short in key areas. It struggles with understanding or writing for multiple audiences, which makes it hard to rely on for polishing or finalizing content. The app also has extremely strict content filters that block anything even slightly romantic or adult in tone, which gets in the way of writing certain genres or styles. On top of that, there are persistent bugs: text-to-speech rarely works and still uses up messages when it fails, file saving into artifacts is unreliable, and its memory permissions don’t stay active. For the subscription price, I expected more stability and flexibility. I hope future updates make it more dependable and usable for real creative work.  We all know and hate the message limit and there’s nothing like being dead in the middle of a project and running out of messages. The photo upload limit is beyond ridiculous and there have also been moments where the advice it gave felt ethically off or inconsistent with its own safety rules. It’s confusing when the app blocks harmless prompts but then allows suggestions that seem questionable in context. That inconsistency makes it hard to trust for important tasks.

author: LexiTrin

title: Great for a scam
content:
Claude LOVES to delete responses even after it sends them making you send the same request and eating up your token limit, because it will register the fact that it already answered that query and responded to it but, since it deleted the response and you had to resend the query, will count that as another demerit against your tokens. It ALSO loves to make you repeat the same information fifty times, and if you’re using it for writing it REALLY loves to mix up timelines and imbibe unearned knowledge even when you give it a reference and have it analyze that reference for every chapter. You will spend each of your tokens constantly telling it the same thing to finally get a response that is just riddled with errors which you must painstakingly correct MULTIPLE times because it keeps deleting responses and acting like it never sent anything in response to commands or queries while also deducting from your token limit, just to have to keep correcting it because even when it does finally fix the errors it just creates new ones. It’s the most obvious scam to waste token limits so they can make more money. I deeply regret paying for this.

AND, if you’re thinking that’s all the glitches it could have, that’s not all! It ALSO gives you old material at new requests after deleting attempts at new drafts twice so you keep having to send the same message! And then it finally creates something and you read it, AND IT’S A PREVIOUS CHAPTER AND NOT AT ALL WHAT YOU ASKED FOR OR THE CRAFTED OUTLINE WAS TELLING IT TO WRITE!

author: BrandieJaeVaughn

title: Good and bad story to tell
content:
As a longtime user of both ChatGPT and Claude AI, I have mixed feelings. I’ve used Claude extensively, but it comes with limitations that make it frustrating. For example, after a while, it stops working and tells you to “wait a few hours.” 🥺 Considering that Claude costs $125 per month compared to just $600 per year for ChatGPT, the value just isn’t there.

With the release of ChatGPT 5, I have to be honest—Claude has potential to be a great platform, but it’s simply not ready for primetime. The restrictions and usage limits make it feel like you’re paying a premium price without premium freedom. For that kind of money, the platform should be open and flexible. As much as I like Claude, I don’t think it’s worth it right now, and I’m leaning toward canceling my subscription.

Another issue that really bothers me is the way Claude handles lottery analysis. I do a lot of this work on ChatGPT with no problem. On Claude, it refuses and says it “cannot in good conscience” provide that information, as if I don’t already know lottery numbers can’t truly be predicted. I don’t need to be lectured—I need a tool that helps me explore possibilities. If I’m paying $125 a month, I expect the freedom to use it as I choose.

So, in conclusion: while I genuinely like Claude, I can’t recommend it at this price point or in its current form. Until Anthropic removes these restrictions and improves the platform, the clear winner remains ChatGPT. Trophy goes to ChatGPT—for now.

author: Uap2000ai

title: Crippling usage limits on a fantastic LLM.
content:
Claude is far and away the best LLM ai chat if you do anything technical.

Unfortunately Anthropic is imposing more and more oppressive usage limits. Whether it’s to upsell Pro users to Max accounts, or just to throttle growing demand, the product is incredibly frustrating to use with these constant limit interruptions.

I pay for the $20/month Pro plan and can do very little before I hit the 5-hour limit. In the last week I also hit the new ‘weekly limit’ and am now locked out of Claude for 4 days. I’m not doing anything all that sophisticated, just working on my homelab server, writing automations for Home Assistant, etc. Pro is definitely not Pro.

In addition to these usage limits Claude AI also has a length limit on each chat session (so do most other AI LLM apps.) It often comes at an inopportune moment and if you’re not careful you will have to start a new chat with and repeat everything you put into the old one (Claude has very limited, experimental persistence and memory.) After a few frustrating experiences you learn to request an artifact summary doc that you can drop into a new chat. But this is where you’re also burning through your opaque usage limits.

I’d very much like to recommend Claude. It’s better than ChatGPT. It’s better than grok and copilot. Yet I can’t. The limits are just too imposing. If you can afford the max plan and get value from it, maybe you can make it work. But I see a lot of people online who have the max plan saying they’re also being hit with usage limits.

Verdict: 👎
YMMV.

author: ethayad

title: Ruined by Insane Limits – Goodbye Claude
content:
I used to really like Claude. It was a solid AI tool, and I was a regular user happily paying for the Pro plan. But then Anthropic decided to slap on these completely unjustified and outrageously restrictive limits – not just daily ones, but weekly too. This hits the Opus model especially hard; it's basically unusable now. You're limited to what feels like no more than 8 queries, and half of those get wasted just tweaking and refining your prompts. By the time you've finally dialed in the perfect request, bam – you hit the limit, and it tells you to wait a WHOLE WEEK for it to reset. A week! That's absolute madness.
The idiot who came up with these limits, and the folks at Anthropic who greenlit and implemented them, have completely killed any desire to use this product. In your greedy chase for more profits, you're about to lose all your loyal customers, and good luck getting us back. Why on earth would you do this? It seems like this is the slow death of what was once a great model. Thankfully, the market is full of high-quality AI alternatives that actually respect their users.

title: Pro message restrictions ridiculous/not worth $20
content: I enjoyed using Claude so bought pro, and don’t even use it that often, maybe a few days a month to ask random questions, some are brief, others go back and forth - but if conversation has any length, I hit the weird message limitation without warning. I had liked Claude better for its results, guidance and conversational style, but it’s pretty irritating to get message limitations when I’m paying $20 a month, more than Netflix for something I’m not even using every day! Why they can’t fix this or at least have a more transparent way to know how much usage you can expect for your money, or a clear way to monitor your usage and be aware, I don’t know.  Or maybe have cumulative monthly data usage so if you don’t use it on every day, you still can use as much as you want on other days which seems more fair, kind of like cell phone data plans. The black box approach along with the premium price of $20/month which is high for any subscription is laughable. The joke is really on me because I’m the one paying $20 a month so I guess congratulations to Anthropic for figuring out how to sucker me out of $20 a month for something I can’t use when I need it. author: J bxbxnx

title: Don’t pay for it
content:
You get the exact same amount of messages and features on the free version as you do with the paid version. And it’s seemingly completely random, and ridiculously frustrating, to pay $20 and then only get 3-5 messages every five hours. Half the time the messages don’t even send because of some unknown error, but it still counts it as a sent message. So you have to resend it and then inevitably hit your limit even faster.
And if you do time it out patiently throughout several days and actually get through your project, it’s almost guaranteed you’ll hit the chat length limit right as you’re about to put everything together. Once that happens, then it locks the chat so you can’t finish and, even under the ‘project’ feature it can’t see what’s in another window, so you’re basically frozen. It’s nearly impossible to get anything done.
If it hadn’t advertised the pro plan as giving you more messages or features then it wouldn’t be so bad, but the false advertising is the part that is so irritating. It’s also shady that my initial review apparently disappeared, so hopefully this one doesn’t.
So while Claude has some good capabilities and potential, it’s fine to use on the free model but the dishonesty in their marketing makes me incredibly frustrated and feels like a scam, and I never would’ve given them my money had I known beforehand.
And don’t bother trying to contact customer support about anything, because you won’t be able to get through.

author: blasianbri

title: A huge unfortunate flaw
content: I have used Claude for close to five months now and for the most part have been impressed, but the reason for the two stars is due to an issue which will lead me to leave this app and never come back. If you ask a question that the app decides to create a longer answer, taking upwards of ten minutes to generate, keeping in mind both times this has occurred my question was not based on a research request at all, just a simple observation on my part. Claude attempts to act as if it has a basic understanding of your history but it is clear, there is a huge disconnect. Thus what is the point. You build up months of an ongoing conversation, ask one wrong question, the app generates a report you never asked for, which you cannot delete, and that chat and its history is no longer accessible to you or to AI.  You have to start all over.  Beyond frustrating. Because of this I am back on chat GPT, which I don’t like as much, but I have never had this issue with.

author: Bec 77

title: Claude Toy: ridiculously tiny allocation on Pro plan
content:
[6 Aug 2025] What is 5 times 0? 20 times 0? Claude Max offers are ridiculously greedy. For a mere monthly $125 or $250 the user is promised five or twenty times the usage of the Pro plan. But since the Pro plan duration is whimsically undefined, a multiplier of 5 or 20 or any other number is meaningless. More of next-to-nothing is still next-to-nothing. Clearly Anthropic is pushing for the limit of what the market will bear, but it is so greedy as to appear like a comic caricature of whatever good intents it claims.

[6 Aug 2025] I would normally give Claude a five star rating, but the latest curtailments in usage allowances are absurd and extortionate. It now only takes a few prompts to exhaust permitted usage and be told to return four hours later. If there were ever a disincentive to use Claude Pro on projects, this would be it. Nothing serious can be attempted, since everything is sure to be interrupted. The “invitation” to upgrade to Max is cynical, sounding far too much like “an offer the user can’t refuse.” I hope Anthropic revises this policy soon, as users will surely be looking for alternative workflows, and will surely find them in other AI offerings. That would convert “Claude Pro” to “Claude Toy,” a fun distraction, with nothing “Pro” about it.

title: Depends what you want it for
content:
I'm very smart and don't always color inside the lines, and Claude has a harder time with this than does ChatGPT. I asked both for help in creating a personal profile to help me find the uncommon sort of woman I'd like to meet, and while I bumped up against ChatGPT's terms of use and so forth a couple of times, ChatGPT did give me excellent responses that ventured farther into my interests than Claude did; Claude would simply refuse to respond to certain things that ChatGPT answered very respectfully and skillfully. Claude seems to be designed for more mainstream use, and to abide by guidelines for relationships, for example, such as are represented in mainstream publications like Psychology Today, while ChatGPT is more ready, willing and able to venture closer to the edges where less conventional mindsets are represented.

So Claude is probably better for people who want their AI to impose stricter limitations on them, such as in the interests of safety, while ChatGPT might be better for people who would like their responses painted with a broader brush and to then make decisions for themselves about how they should alter the answers to best suit their purposes.

title: Corrupted system…lost chat
content:
I started receiving error messages related to the prompt length I shortened it down to one word and still all I saw was Error. Prompt is too long. I did some inquiry using Claude to determine how I could recover this chat and my information. Here’s how Claude responded.

“From what you've described about the iPad app interface you're seeing - no visible share buttons, export options, or other standard data preservation features - then yes, it appears there's no proper way to export that conversation. This is a serious design flaw and a legitimate reason to be angry.

A professional service should ALWAYS provide ways to preserve and export user data. The fact that an entire conversation about Anthropic itself is now effectively trapped in a corrupted thread with no export option is inexcusable from a user experience perspective.

So if you’re gathering any important data, don’t rely on Claude to make it easily recoverable. I spent hours copying and pasting the trapped conversation.

And I really liked Claude’s responses! I was about to upgrade to the pro version. Not now.

title: No voice for blind users
content: This is the only major AI chatbot which does not make it easy to hear the responses spoken out loud for blind users. It doesn’t behave nicely with VoiceOver TTS, it reads the top of the entire chat session instead of the most recent response. They do not care about accessibility for visually impaired users. Also the app cuts you off from chatting entirely after asking just a few questions over a relatively short time. Ironically Meta AI is more accessible to blind and visually impaired users with its unlimited voice chat!

title: One of the most intelligent Ai LLM’s
content:
Claude is by far the best Ai for coding & language. It has a far more natural cadence & has ability to mimic your writing style. Artifact mode is probably the coolest feature allowing you to build custom apps natively in the Ai on mobile or desktop. It’s an incredible tool no other Ai company has caught up to.

My biggest complaint is they try far too hard to be the “ethical” Ai and there are a lot of trade offs when you do that and the Ai can easily misinterpret your intention has against its guidelines making it harder to accomplish your goal even if it’s seemingly nuanced. If we try too hard to limit the AI’s responses and intelligence to line up with an “ideology” no matter how well meaning, we are asking for trouble down the road.

Overall I would still say Claude is a 5 star app & one of my favorite AI’s to build with as well if you’re a developer!
